*Do-the-job track · Job A of 3.*

Before trusting Gaussianization on real data, calibrate it where the answer is
known.  The deliverable is a **calibration sheet**: estimator vs truth, and a
RBIG round-trip / tail check.

---

## 1 · MI Estimator vs the Closed Form

```{python}
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
print(f"{'ρ':>5}{'exact MI':>11}{'estimate':>11}{'abs err':>9}")
print("-" * 36)
for r in [0.0, 0.3, 0.6, 0.8, 0.9]:
    xy = rng.multivariate_normal([0, 0], [[1, r], [r, 1]], size=5000)
    exact = -0.5 * np.log(1 - r**2)
    est = mutual_information_xy(xy[:, 0], xy[:, 1], bins=24)
    print(f"{r:>5.1f}{exact:>11.3f}{est:>11.3f}{abs(est-exact):>9.3f}")
```

The error is dominated by the bias floor at ρ = 0; subtract that and the estimate
is trustworthy.

---

## 2 · RBIG: Forward Decorrelates, Backward Preserves the Tail

```{python}
a, b = datasets.tail_dependent_pair(n=2000, seed=4)
X = np.column_stack([a, b])
rbig = AnnealedRBIG(n_layers=30, random_state=0).fit(X)
Z = rbig.transform(X)
gen = rbig.sample(2000)

print(f"forward  |corr|:  {abs(np.corrcoef(a,b)[0,1]):.3f}  →  "
      f"{abs(np.corrcoef(Z[:,0],Z[:,1])[0,1]):.3f}   (decorrelated)")
print(f"backward co-crash: real {cocrash_fraction(a,b):.0%}  vs  "
      f"sample {cocrash_fraction(gen[:,0],gen[:,1]):.0%}   (tail preserved)")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-jobA-calibration
#| fig-cap: "Calibration at a glance: estimate vs exact MI (left); marginal of the forward pass is standard normal (right)."
from scipy.stats import norm
fig, (axL, axR) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 4.2))

rhos = np.linspace(0, 0.9, 10)
truth = [-0.5 * np.log(1 - r**2) for r in rhos]
est = [mutual_information_xy(*rng.multivariate_normal([0, 0], [[1, r], [r, 1]],
       size=4000).T, bins=24) for r in rhos]
axL.plot(rhos, truth, c=INK, lw=2.2, label="exact")
axL.plot(rhos, est, "o", c=COOL, label="estimate")
axL.set_xlabel("ρ"); axL.set_ylabel("MI (nats)"); axL.legend(fontsize=9, frameon=False)
axL.set_title("MI calibration", fontsize=12); despine(axL)

grid = np.linspace(-4, 4, 200)
axR.hist(Z[:, 0], bins=40, density=True, color=plotting.PALETTE["green"], alpha=0.8)
axR.plot(grid, norm.pdf(grid), c=INK, lw=2)
axR.set_title("forward marginal ≈ N(0,1)", fontsize=12); despine(axR)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## The Deliverable
A one-page sheet: "MI estimator within a few hundredths of a nat of the closed
form after floor subtraction; RBIG decorrelates to |corr| < 0.05 and regenerates
the co-crash to within a few points." That is your license to use it on real data.
